top_news.title: Simplifying Model Serving Across Multiple GPUs with NVIDIA TensorRT Multi-Device Integration in NVIDIA Dynamo-Triton
top_news.dek: NVIDIA TensorRT 11.0 introduces multi-device inference, allowing a single network to execute across multiple GPUs using NCCL-backed distributed collectives.
top_news.brief: This update addresses memory and compute constraints for large generative AI models by enabling distributed execution. By leveraging NCCL, TensorRT maintains its inference optimizations while scaling across multiple GPUs. The feature is integrated into the NVIDIA Dynamo-Triton inference server.
top_news.image_alt: Diagram showing a single TensorRT network distributed across multiple GPU nodes.

top_news.title: US and China agree on AI dialogue with security mechanism ahead of Trump-Xi summit
top_news.dek: The US and China have agreed to establish an official AI dialogue and a notification mechanism for national security-related AI incidents.
top_news.brief: Ahead of the upcoming summit between Donald Trump and Xi Jinping, US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent and Chinese Vice Premier He Lifeng announced the framework. The initiative aims to manage risks associated with AI development through formal communication channels.
top_news.image_alt: US and Chinese flags side by side.

top_news.title: Kev: Tiny Jev-like family of decision models built on top of Qwen3.5
top_news.dek: Kev is a new family of small, Jev-inspired decision-making models fine-tuned on Qwen3.5 for local training and execution.
top_news.brief: Designed for task-specific decision-making, the Kev models are available in 0.8B, 4B, and 9B parameter sizes. The project provides a framework for developers to train and deploy these compact models on their own infrastructure.
top_news.image_alt: GitHub repository badge showing model weights for Kev 0.8B, 4B, and 9B.
